newsitem.title: GERMANY: Alusaf smelter costs seen setting pace for others.
newsitem.headline: Alusaf smelter costs seen setting pace for others.

text.p: Alusaf Pty Ltd's new Hillside smelter had a competitive cost structure and new projects would have to be measured against it, said John Barter of Canadian plant builder SNC Lavalin Inc.
The smelter, which came on stream in June 1995, is the most recent western world green-field capacity addition.
Barter, who was addressing a Metal Bulletin conference, said $1.4 billion for a 466,000 tonne a year plant meant new capacity costs of $3,050 per tonne.
The figure included construction, engineering, and all direct owners' costs, but not power generation or ocean port infrastructure costs.
Barter said higher costs in current or future projects elsewhere needed to be offset through lower power rates, proximity to final markets or other favourable operating parameters.

The smelter is expected to raise production at Alusaf, a unit of Gencor Ltd to 665,000 tonnes in the year to June 30, 1997 from 173,960 tonne at Bayside and 237,619 tonnes at Hillside in the year ended in June 1996, the company said last month.
Day-to-day production costs at Hillside are estimated at well below the market average of $1,500 a tonne, an analyst at the conference said.
